title: 10 Essential Kitchen Appliances Every Modern Home Needs
summary: Explore the best kitchen appliances for Bangladeshi households, including refrigerators, rice cookers, kettles, induction cookers, air fryers, ovens, blenders, and more.
intro: Discover the essential kitchen appliances for Bangladeshi homes, from fridges to rice cookers.
html:
Kitchen appliances have moved from "nice to have" to essential infrastructure in most Bangladeshi households. Rising dual-income families, smaller kitchen footprints in apartments, and frequent gas line disruptions have all pushed buyers toward appliances that cook faster, use less manual effort, and don't depend entirely on a gas stove. This guide breaks down the appliances worth buying first, what specs actually matter when comparing models, and where to find each category in Bangladesh.

1. REFRIGERATOR

A fridge is one of the most important appliances in any modern kitchen because it runs 24/7 and plays a central role in storing vegetables, meat, fish, dairy products, drinks, and leftover food. Families mostly buy these groceries on a weekly or monthly basis and often feel the need for a deep freezer aside from their regular refrigerator. So when comparing refrigerators, popular brands, pay attention to capacity, energy efficiency, compressor technology, and freezer configuration.

A 200–250L single-door refrigerator from Singer can work well for a couple or small household, while families of four or more may prefer 300L or larger double-door or side-by-side models with separate freezer compartments from LG.

What to check: Capacity, inverter compressor, energy consumption, frost-free operation, freezer layout, vegetable storage, warranty, and service availability. See our refrigerator buying guide.

2. RICE COOKER

Rice is a daily staple for many Bangladeshi households, which makes a rice cooker one of the most useful appliances to own. A rice cooker removes the two most common failure points of stovetop rice, which are burning the bottom layer and misjudging water ratios. Basic models are designed primarily for rice, while more advanced models can include settings for khichuri, porridge, steaming, or other dishes.

Capacity should match the number of people you normally cook for. A 1.5L model can be suitable for a small household, while larger 1.8L–2.8L models are more ideal for bigger families or households that regularly cook larger quantities.

What to check: Capacity, inner-pot quality, cooking modes, keep-warm function, steaming capability, and replacement-pot availability.

3. ELECTRIC KETTLE

An electric kettle is one of the simplest time-saving appliances for making tea, coffee, hot water, or instant meals. It boils water in roughly 3-4 minutes, whereas a gas stove takes 8-10 minutes. For most households, a 1.5–1.8L kettle is a suitable size. Smaller models suit one or two people, while larger capacities make more sense when several people regularly need hot water.

What to check: Capacity, wattage, automatic shut-off, boil-dry protection, handle design, material, and warranty.

4. GAS STOVE OR ELECTRIC COOKER

Gas stoves remain very common in Bangladeshi homes, but the recent low line pressure during peak cooking hours is slowing daily meal preparations. That is why induction is now the reliable gas alternative in Bangladesh. Induction cookers are currently the popular type of electric cooker that heats the pan directly through electromagnetic induction. 

The second option is the infrared cooker that uses a heating coil or plate. It works with any flat-bottom pot, but it heats slowly and stays hot after you switch it off. A gas stove gives instant flame control, yet it depends on a steady pipeline gas supply and LPG cylinder availability. Induction sits between the two. It offers the speed of gas and the plug-in convenience of an electric cooker. These cooktops are available from many brands, but most shoppers in Bangladesh are often found comparing models from Philips with Oraimo before buying.

Related Blog: Induction Cooker vs Infrared Cooker: Which One Should You Buy in Bangladesh?

What to check: Wattage, temperature and power controls, cookware compatibility, safety features, timer, display, and electrical requirements.

5. AIR FRYER

The air fryer has become one of the fastest-growing appliance categories in Bangladesh. It is useful for households that frequently prepare fried or roasted foods but want to use significantly less added oil than traditional deep frying. Hot air circulates around the food to create browning and crispness. Depending on the recipe, little or no additional oil may be necessary. If you need complete guidelines to choose the best air fryer for your home, read our dedicated blog on it here.

At a glance, premium brands like Philips usually come with advanced features to reduce oil usage, while affordable air fryer brands like Oraimo offer great models. Beyond health benefits, it's also considerably faster to clean since there's no oil to strain, cool, and store afterward.

What to check: Basket capacity, temperature range, power rating, basket design, controls, cleaning convenience, and warranty.

6. MICROWAVE OR CONVECTION OVEN

An oven is particularly useful for reheating food, defrosting frozen ingredients, and quickly heating drinks or prepared meals. In most Bangladeshi kitchens, a microwave-convection combo oven is the value-for-money choice, since it can handle multiple cooking and food processing needs.

The question of which oven is suitable for your home ultimately depends on how you use the appliance. Around 20L can be sufficient for basic reheating and smaller households, while larger 25–32L+ models provide more room for baking dishes and larger portions. Ovens from Whirlpool and Samsung are some of the most popular brands you can trust in Bangladesh.

What to check: Type, capacity, power, temperature control, convection mode, grill function, rack positions, and warranty.

7. BLENDER & GRINDER

A blender & grinder covers a wider range of daily kitchen tasks than almost any other appliance on this list. Smoothies, lassi, chutneys, spice grinding, and bhorta pastes all go through the same jar. Multiple jars are particularly useful. A wet jar can be dedicated to liquids and smoothies, while a smaller dry or chutney jar can be used for spices and pastes. This appliance also helps prevent strong smells from transferring between different ingredients.

Panasonic and Havells are brands we can confidently suggest as the best blenders available in the Bangladeshi marketplace due to their durable stainless steel blades, secure jar locking, easy-to-clean components, and a motor designed for the type of work you expect to do.

What to check: Motor power, jar capacity, number of jars, blade material, speed settings, pulse function, and overload protection.

8. JUICER

A dedicated juicer separates pulp and fiber far more cleanly than trying to force fruit through a regular blender, which is why it's worth the separate purchase if fresh juice is a daily habit rather than an occasional treat. For daily use with fruits like oranges or pomegranates, a centrifugal juicer is usually the most suitable and affordable starting point. Cold-press models are better suited to leafy greens and anyone prioritizing juice quality over speed.

What to check: Juicing method, feed-chute size, pulp container, cleaning requirements, motor power, noise level, and compatible produce.

9. KITCHEN GEYSER

A kitchen geyser supplies you with hot water at the sink within seconds. It saves homemakers from boiling a kettle for every dish, pot, or cup of tea. In Bangladesh, winter mornings and greasy cookware make hot water a daily need. A small geyser easily fits under or beside the sink and connects to the existing cold water line.

There are instant geysers and storage geysers. So before you buy, you must learn about the difference between an instant and a storage geyser. Brand choice matters too. Haier offers a wide range of compact electric water heaters for homes. TESY makes tank models known for good insulation and stable temperature control.

What to check: Capacity, wattage, heating time, temperature control, safety valve, tank material, water pressure rating, and electrical requirements.

10. DISHWASHER

A dishwasher is a less essential appliance than a refrigerator or rice cooker, but it can be extremely useful for joint families, especially in apartments where saving time on daily chores is a priority. Dishwashers use a combination of spraying, detergent, heat, and filtration to clean dishes.

Beyond convenience, dishwashers from brands like Sharp and Hitachi typically use less water per wash cycle than hand-washing the same load, since the water is recirculated and filtered rather than run continuously from the tap.

What to check: Place settings, water consumption, noise level, wash programs, drying system, dimensions, installation requirements, and warranty/service.

How to Prioritize: Which One to Buy First

You will initially not need all ten appliances when setting up a new kitchen. The right order actually depends on your budget and cooking habits. If you are starting from scratch, prioritize appliances based on how essential they are for your everyday cooking, not simply the order in which they appear above.

Tier 1: Everyday Essentials

  • Refrigerator: For storing fresh and cooked food.
  • Rice cooker: Particularly useful as rice is part of our daily meals.
  • Electric kettle: Convenient for tea, coffee, hot water, and quick meals.
  • Induction cooker: A useful alternative cooking option, particularly when gas supply is unreliable.

Tier 2: Highly useful additions

  • Blender & grinder: Useful for spices, sauces, drinks, chutneys, and pastes.
  • Microwave/convection oven: Especially valuable for reheating and defrosting, with additional baking/grilling capability on suitable models.
  • Air fryer: Worth considering if you regularly prepare fried or roasted foods.

Tier 3: Lifestyle-based appliances

  • Dishwasher: A major convenience upgrade for households that want to reduce the time spent washing dishes.
  • Kitchen Geyser: Makes sense for homes with babies and elderly citizens.
  • Juicer: Best for households that regularly prepare fresh juice.

How to Choose Appliances for Your Household

  • Before buying a kitchen appliance, focus on how often you'll use it, how much space you have, and whether it actually solves your daily chores.
  • Match it to your cooking habits: A rice cooker and blender may be your top priorities if you are regular in cooking Bengali meals.
  • Choose the right capacity: Don't pay extra for oversized appliances you rarely fill. Consider your family size and typical portions.
  • Check kitchen space: Measure your counter, cabinet, and storage space before buying, especially for refrigerators, ovens, and dishwashers.
  • Consider electricity use: Check wattage and energy-efficiency information, particularly for appliances that run frequently or use heating elements.
  • Think about reliability and service: For refrigerators, ovens, cookers, and other expensive appliances, warranty coverage, spare parts, and local after-sales service matter.
  • Prioritize essentials first: Buy appliances that you are going to need regularly, then add convenience or specialty appliances as your needs and budget allow.
  • The best appliance isn't necessarily the most powerful or expensive one; it's the one that fits your household, kitchen, and everyday routine.

Building Your Kitchen The Smart Way

You don't need to buy every appliance on this list at once. Just start with the essentials that match how you actually cook and eat, then add specialized appliances as your kitchen habits become clearer. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQS)

Question-1:

Which kitchen appliance should I buy first for a new apartment?

A refrigerator is usually the first priority because it is essential for safely storing fresh and cooked food. After that, choose appliances based on your cooking habits. A rice cooker, electric kettle, and induction cooker are common priorities for many Bangladeshi households.

Question-2:

Is an air fryer or a microwave oven more useful for a small kitchen?

An air fryer is better suited to frying-style cooking with less oil, while a microwave-convection oven covers reheating, defrosting, and baking. If counter space is limited, a combo oven generally covers more use cases than an air fryer alone.

Question-3:

Do induction cookers work with all cookware?

No. Induction cooktops only heat ferromagnetic cookware such as cast iron or induction-compatible stainless steel. Aluminum, copper, and glass pots won't work unless they have a magnetic base layer.

Question-4:

How much electricity do kitchen appliances like a fridge or induction cooker use?

A refrigerator operates continuously, so its inverter compressor and steady energy consumption are important for long-term electricity costs. An induction cooker uses more power while operating, but it typically runs for much shorter periods.
